original_question: Is every biharmonic hypersurface of a Euclidean space minimal?
target_in_paper: Section 10.1, Conjecture 3 (the original biharmonic conjecture): the paper’s official statement is that the only biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces are the minimal ones; your draft asks the codimension-one (hypersurface) special case of this conjecture. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Euclidean ambient setting, the biharmonic hypothesis, and the minimality conclusion. It matches the main rigidity direction discussed in Sections 9–11, but it narrows the paper’s official conjecture from all submanifolds to hypersurfaces. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is broader: Conjecture 3 concerns every biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space, not only hypersurfaces. So your draft captures a special case rather than the exact statement in the paper. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The geometric setup should be stated explicitly as an isometric immersion x:M^n→E^{n+1} of a connected Riemannian manifold into real Euclidean space; this is the ambient notation used in the paper. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The term “biharmonic” should be defined. In Section 9, for an immersion x:M→E^m, this means Δ^2x=0, equivalently ΔH=0, where Δ is the Laplace operator on M and H is the mean curvature vector. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The quantifier over dimensions is implicit in your draft. To be stand-alone and paper-faithful, it should say that the question is asked for every n-dimensional Euclidean hypersurface M^n⊂E^{n+1}. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
The conclusion “minimal” should be made explicit as H≡0 identically. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The conjecture as stated does not impose completeness, compactness, or properness; those assumptions appear only in later partial results supporting the conjecture. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
refined_question: Hypersurface case of Chen’s original biharmonic conjecture: let x:M^n→E^{n+1} be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian hypersurface into real Euclidean space. If x is biharmonic, in the sense that Δ^2x=0 (equivalently ΔH=0), where Δ is the Laplace operator on M and H is the mean curvature vector, must H vanish identically? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if the inclusion map ι:M^n→E^{n+1} is a biharmonic map, must the hypersurface be minimal? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
justification: Section 9 defines biharmonic submanifolds extrinsically by Δ^2x=0, equivalently ΔH=0, and also identifies this with the inclusion map being biharmonic. Section 10.1 then states the official open problem as Conjecture 3. Because the paper does not formulate a separate hypersurface-only conjecture, the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite of your draft is the codimension-one specialization of Conjecture 3 with the Section 9 notation made explicit. Section 11, Remark 1 records that Conjecture 3 remains open. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
